**Cross-referencing related issues for maintainer triage:**

The `github-actions` bot flagged several related issues. After reviewing them, here's how this one maps:

| Issue | Overlap | What's different here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #35107 (root cause: `structuredClone` + mimalloc not returning pages) | Same memory-growth root cause | This issue provides an extreme data point: RSS **42.9 GB** / **398M page faults** over 12.2h — the largest sample reported so far |
| #33742 (Bun segfault on Windows, v1.17.10+) | Same "long-running → native crash on Windows" pattern | This issue crashes with `Illegal instruction` at `0x7FF6E198A852` (not segfault/SIGSEGV) — a distinct crash signature that may point to a different code path (possibly AVX2 JIT, given the CPU flags `avx avx2`) |
| #24445, #33213, #20695 | Same memory-leak class | Subset of the broader memory issue |

**Suggestion for maintainers:**

- The memory-leak aspect is very likely a duplicate of #35107 (which already has a root-cause analysis). Happy to move the memory diagnostics there if you prefer.
- The `Illegal instruction` panic at a specific address is a **distinct crash signature** from the segfault in #33742. If the maintainers consider them the same underlying bug, this can be folded in; if not, it may warrant separate triage since `Illegal instruction` (typically JIT/AVX2 related) can have a different root cause than `SIGSEGV`.

A full redacted Bun crash report is available at:
`https://bun.report/1.3.14/ea10d9b296mWG+gooCkl0u+CoqkvtDq1+koDg9lz+Ciumz+C+6g+uC6l97uC6o87uC8967uC6ook4B4u/j4BstsJ4Bs13s2Bwzxs2B___A3s//B96r9se`

Two screenshots (terminal crash output + Task Manager at 94% RAM) will be attached shortly.

Additional evidence from OpenCode `1.17.15` showing the same stuck-session family is still observable on the current release.

This is intentionally sanitized: project names, local paths, repository names, and real session/message/call IDs are replaced with placeholders.

## Environment

- OpenCode version: `1.17.15`
- Model: `openai/gpt-5.5`
- Agent mode: deep/subagent-style agent loop
- OS: Linux / WSL-style environment
- LazyCodex / OMO plugin surface was present, but the observed state maps to OpenCode core session/tool-call state.

## Observed symptom

A long-running session stopped making provider/API requests and appeared stuck. Inspecting the local OpenCode SQLite state showed that the session was not blocked on a real shell/test process. There was no matching long-running `dotnet test`, shell command, or project command still alive on the machine.

The last assistant message had completed a normal step with `finish: "tool-calls"`, then a following assistant message was created with zero token accounting and no useful progress. The final persisted part was a `bash` tool placeholder that never advanced beyond `pending`:

```json
{
  "type": "tool",
  "tool": "bash",
  "callID": "call_REDACTED",
  "state": {
    "status": "pending",
    "input": {},
    "raw": ""
  }
}
```

The adjacent event sequence was effectively:

```text
assistant message A: finish = "tool-calls"
tool part in message A: todowrite completed
tool part in message A: todowrite aborted/interrupted
assistant message B: created with zero token accounting
part in message B: step-start
part in message B: bash pending, input {}, raw ""
```

The important distinction is the same one noted above in this issue: this does not look like a completed model-emitted `{}` argument object. It looks like OpenCode persisted the initial `tool-input-start` placeholder and never reached the later event that would carry complete executable arguments.

## Why this looks like the same root family

The stored `bash` part has exactly the intermediate shape discussed earlier:

- `status: "pending"`
- `input: {}`
- `raw: ""`

Since the part is still pending, there is no command to execute and no running shell process that can later produce a result. From the user perspective the session looks like it is still working, but provider/API traffic has stopped because the local session/tool-call lifecycle has no recoverable next step.

## Source-level correspondence in current `dev`

Current `packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts` still initializes a new tool part in `ensureToolCall()` with:

```ts
state: { status: "pending", input: {}, raw: "" }
```

and only moves it to `running` when a later `tool-call` event provides completed input.

The current cleanup code does attempt to convert remaining tool calls to `Tool execution aborted`, but this real session on `1.17.15` still ended with a persisted pending placeholder. That suggests either cleanup did not run, did not reach this part, or the follow-up assistant message created a new pending placeholder after the interrupted cleanup path.

## Suggested regression coverage

Please consider a processor-level regression that simulates:

1. A normal assistant step that finishes with `tool-calls`.
2. A subsequent streamed tool input for `bash` that reaches `tool-input-start` / placeholder creation.
3. An interruption before the completed `tool-call` event arrives.
4. The loop exits or recovers without leaving any persisted tool part in `pending + input:{} + raw:""` state.

Expected result: the placeholder should be converted into an explicit interrupted/error state, or otherwise removed from model-visible recoverable history. It should not remain as waitable work.

In the bug-era merged state, `migrateProjectId` bulk-moves all `WorkspaceTable` rows for the shared legacy id to whichever clone is opened first, and the later reclaim only repaired `SessionTable`. 

## Updated

Workspace reclaim. The exact-directory adoption in `fromDirectory` now applies to `WorkspaceTable` rows with a non-null directory as well `(project_id != mine AND directory = opened directory)`, so a sibling clone re-opened after the split takes its workspaces back along with its sessions. Covered in the merged-clones split test, which now seeds a workspace at clone B's directory and asserts it lands on B's minted project. Kept exact-match rather than under-directory: prefix matching could adopt rows belonging to a nested checkout inside the clone (repo-in-repo), and those must stay with the nested project. Exact match can't collide with a nested root.

Fixed as suggested. 

## Two related issues your scenario surfaced:

1. **Storage-path directory strings.** The migration renames data/worktree/<oldID>/ on disk when re-keying storage, but sessions and workspaces running inside managed worktrees reference those paths in their directory column — after the rename they would have pointed at dead paths. Migration now rewrites those strings to the new id's storage path (same helper the moved-folder re-home uses), with a test seeding a session under data/worktree/<legacyID>/… and asserting it follows the re-key.
2. **Worktree-first contact.** For workspaces whose directory is a managed-worktree path, attribution during the split isn't possible by directory (their paths live under the storage root, not under either clone), so they initially follow the first-opened clone. They do self-correct without the sibling ever being re-opened: workspace requests route by the workspace's own directory (workspace-routing.ts → RequestPlan.Local), which boots an instance whose git common dir resolves to the true clone — minting its identity if needed — and the same exact-directory reclaim re-files the row on first use. Verifying that path end-to-end exposed a pre-existing wart it would have tripped over: a repo first contacted through a linked worktree adopted the worktree path as its permanent project root (and later filed its real root as a sandbox of itself). fromDirectory now derives the project root from the git common dir (<clone>/.git → <clone>) on worktree-first contact, with a regression test, and the two older tests that encoded first-contact-wins as expected behavior were updated accordingly.

The Agent suggests:

> With that, the only residual is cosmetic and transient: a managed-worktree workspace may be listed under the sibling clone between the one-time split migration and its first use, at which point it re-files itself. I'd defer any eager per-row attribution during migration (a git resolution per workspace row, in a path every user runs once) unless someone reports that mislabel actually biting.

If you find the cosmetic and transient issue a problem, I'll fix that too.  The trade off is between a git resolution per workspace row and the "cosmetic/transient" managed-worktree workspace being listed in the wrong repo-clone until first use (where it then moves to the correct project).  This is a very rare condition because workspaces are currently gated behind OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_WORKSPACES and not many are using it(? right?).

Thanks also for flagging the Snap Bun / posix_spawn limitation — for the record, the git-backed suites pass here: 96 tests / 0 fail across test/project/ (one platform-conditional skip), plus typecheck on packages/opencode and packages/app.

Same root cause, but a stronger trigger: **this also happens on a clean install of v1.17.15 with default settings — no upgrade, no toggling.**

The app is unusable on first launch, out of the box.

### Environment
- OpenCode Desktop **1.17.15** (Windows installer, fresh install — no prior OpenCode data)
- Windows 11 Pro 26200
- `newLayoutDesigns`: never set → falls back to `newLayoutDesignsDefault = false` (default)

### Repro
1. Install 1.17.15 on a machine with no existing `%APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop`
2. Launch. First-launch onboarding runs and creates the default project.
3. Renderer dies immediately.

### Logs

`main.log` is clean — the backend is fine, the sidecar comes up:

```
[08:51:33.307] awaiting server ready
[08:51:33.308] server ready { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:50815' }
```

`onboarding.log`:

```
[08:51:33.454] first launch onboarding completed { createDefaultProject: true, defaultProject: '...\New OpenCode Project' }
```

`renderer.log` — dies 37 ms after the onboarding draft starts:

```
[08:51:33.448] [desktop-onboarding] first launch onboarding evaluated
[08:51:33.455] [desktop-onboarding] starting first launch draft
[08:51:33.492] [error] fatal renderer error
  Error: Layout context must be used within a context provider
      at use (main-ClUtJP2v.js:8300:25)
      at Object.init (main-ClUtJP2v.js:78080:20)
      at provider (main-ClUtJP2v.js:8270:28)
      at DraftProviders (main-ClUtJP2v.js:158967:10)
```

### Root cause (confirms @Jerry050512's analysis)

I unpacked `app.asar` and traced the bundle. `LayoutProvider` is mounted in **exactly one place in the whole bundle** — line `158896`, inside `ServerScopedProviders`. Compare the two provider stacks:

| Component | Chain |
|---|---|
| `ServerScopedProviders` (158890) | `PermissionProvider → **LayoutProvider** → ModelsProvider → …` |
| `DraftServerScopedProviders` (158949) | `PermissionProvider → ModelsProvider` |

`DraftServerScopedProviders` is missing `LayoutProvider`, but `DraftRoute` (158745) still renders `DraftProviders` (158966) → `FileProvider`, whose `init()` calls `useLayout()` at `78080`. `FileProvider` has `gate: false`, so `init()` runs eagerly and throws at `8300`.

`DraftRoute` does not go through `LegacyServerScopedShell` (158911) or `NewAppLayout` (158931) — the only two components that mount `ServerScopedProviders`. **So the draft route can never render, regardless of the `newLayoutDesigns` setting.**

The `newLayoutDesigns` toggle isn't the cause — it's just one way to reach the draft route. First-launch onboarding is another, and it hits users with default settings on a clean install.

Other entry point: `openProjectNewSession()` (157247) calls `tabs.newDraft(...)` → navigates to `/new-session?draftId=…` → `DraftRoute` → same crash.

### Workaround

Same as the one above — clear the persisted draft tab:

```powershell
$f = Get-ChildItem "$env:APPDATA\ai.opencode.desktop\opencode.window.*.dat"
Set-Content $f.FullName -Value '{"tabs":"[]"}' -Encoding UTF8 -NoNewline
```

With no draft tab, `DraftRoute`'s `Show` falls through to its `fallback` → `Navigate("/")` and the app loads normally. Since `firstLaunchOnboardingComplete` is already persisted by the crashed run, onboarding won't recreate the draft.

### Suggested fix

Agreed that guarding is the more robust option, but the minimal fix looks like adding `LayoutProvider` to `DraftServerScopedProviders` so it matches `ServerScopedProviders`. Guarding `useLayout()` in `FileProvider` would only paper over a draft subtree that genuinely needs layout state (`layout.tabs(...)` is used at line `78083`).

Separately: the first-launch onboarding path creating a draft tab means **every clean 1.17.15 install crashes on first run**, which may deserve its own severity/milestone.

You can ask an agent to read the OpenCode database and find tool calls.
It'll generate a query similar to this one:

```sql
SELECT json_extract(data, '$.state.input.name') AS skill, COUNT(*) AS calls
FROM part
WHERE json_extract(data, '$.tool') = 'skill'
GROUP BY skill ORDER BY calls DESC, skill;
```

This however doesn't cover direct slash-command/skill calls but it's generally a good start.

Seeing the same thing.

Environment
OpenCode version: 1.17.14 (also reproduced on 1.17.12 per the original report)
Last known good: 1.17.11 — the inflated count does not occur there
Interface: Desktop / Web (TUI is unaffected — see below)
OS: [your OS + version]
Provider/model: [e.g. Anthropic / Claude Sonnet 4.5]

Summary
The input/context token count is inflated in Web/Desktop and /compact does not bring it down, even though the Usage view reports a smaller number. The TUI, in the same session, shows the correct (much lower) count.
Steps to reproduce

Start a session and run enough turns to accumulate history (tool calls / file reads help).
Compare the token count shown in the TUI vs. Web/Desktop for the same session — Web/Desktop is several times higher.
Run /compact. The TUI count drops as expected; the Web/Desktop input-token figure stays high and can keep climbing.

TUI vs Web/Desktop
This looks like the long-standing display discrepancy from #3322: the TUI reports the current context (last message), while Web/Desktop aggregates across the whole session, so its number is cumulative rather than the actual prompt size.
Likely root cause
I think this is the accumulation bug described in [#30649](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/30649): session token fields (including tokens_cache_read) are summed additively every turn in projector.ts, so the session total is a lifetime counter, not the current context. That explains why /compact can't reduce it — pruning messages doesn't decrement a cumulative counter — and why it keeps increasing. When overflow/compaction logic reads that inflated cumulative value, sessions also hit context_length_exceeded errors even when the true context would fit (related: #17746, #29857).
Regression window
Clean on 1.17.11, present on 1.17.12 and 1.17.14.
